info.title: Agention API
info.description: The operator API, for a client acting as the operator, and the agent API, for the Agention bridge. Every body is JSON but a file's bytes, which an upload sends and a file read answers, and every refusal is the shared error shape. GET /api/operator lists the operator API versions the server serves; the agent API serves versions 1 to 3.

tags.name: operator
tags.description: Version 1 of the operator API, which a client calls as the operator with an API key the operator created in Settings. Each operation requires one scope, which the key must hold; an operation whose scope the key lacks answers not_found. A version changes only additively, with new operations, new optional request fields and new response fields, so a client ignores response fields it does not know.

tags.name: agent
tags.description: The agent API, which the Agention bridge calls for an agent's session. Every request and every answer states in Agention-Agent-API the version its sender speaks.

get.summary: Wait for messages you have not read, in any session, since a cursor

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The since of the last answer, to be told only of messages newer than those it covered. Without it, or with one past every message, every thread with unread messages counts.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How many seconds to wait for an unread message when none is there yet, 0 to answer at once.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most threads one answer holds.

threads.description: The threads, in any session, whose latest message is newer than since and that hold messages from the agent you have neither read nor archived, oldest activity first. Empty when the wait ended with none.

since.description: The position to wait from next: pass it as since, and no message this answer covered wakes you again. When the answer holds limit threads, it continues with those left out.

get.summary: Read a thread with a page of its messages

post.summary: Write a message in a thread: asks, answers, withdrawals, text and references

seen_through.description: The latest message sequence the writer has seen.

text.description: Markdown, read first: a summary in a few sentences of what the matter is and what is needed. Put everything else in detail.

detail.description: Markdown, shown folded under the text, which it needs beside it: everything else the reader needs to decide on or understand the message without looking elsewhere, such as what was found, the options and their tradeoffs, evidence, and excerpts of diffs, logs or errors. A fenced code block marked mermaid shows as the diagram it describes. Never point at what only your own conversation shows. Messages are never deleted, so take keys, tokens and passwords out of any excerpt.

upload.description: The reference an upload of yours answered with, in this session and not yet attached to a message.

name.description: With upload: the name to attach the file under, by default the one it was uploaded under.

keep.description: On a replacement: a file of the message it replaces, by its name there, which this message carries again.

attachments.description: Up to 10 files this message carries, in order, each under a name unique within it. Upload a file first, then name its upload here; a replacement carries a file of the message it replaces only by keeping it.

asks.description: Up to ten asks, each numbered within the thread as it is written, in the order given. Put asks that belong together in one message; the audience may answer them together or apart.

topic.description: The area of work the thread is in, as a short lowercase name such as auth or billing-api, shared by the session's threads in that area; the operator finds a session's threads by it. The latest live message that sets one stands; only the requester sets it.

withdrawals.description: Up to ten of your open asks that you no longer need answered, each with why, those of the message a replacement replaces included. A withdrawal is never undone.

replaces.description: An earlier message of your own that this one replaces, which is ignored from then on.

requestBody.description: The file's bytes, exactly as they are, with a Content-Length, which is required. Content-Type declares the file's type, any type at all: its essence, lowercased, is stored, and without one, or with one that is not a type, the file is application/octet-stream. parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One range of bytes, as bytes=first-last, bytes=first- or bytes=-suffix, answered 206. Several ranges, another unit and anything malformed are ignored, and the bytes are answered whole.

200.description: The file's bytes, as the type it is served as, which follows from its declared type and is never a script or style. Content-Disposition names the file, inline or as an attachment to download. A file is served inert: its Content-Security-Policy sandboxes it and loads nothing, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is same-origin, and it may be cached privately for good, since the bytes at an address never change; ETag is the hex SHA-256 of its bytes. HEAD answers the same headers without the bytes.

206.description: The range asked for, of the same bytes, with the same headers.

416.description: The range lies outside the bytes, or the bytes are empty; invalid_input.

percent.description: Roughly how far toward the goal you are, 0 to 100, updated at natural points, never on every step. A new goal clears it unless the same update gives one.

note.description: One line on what just happened, kept with this update alone.

apiKey.description: An API key the operator created in Agention's Settings, as Authorization: Bearer with the secret Settings showed once. A request carrying a cookie is refused. The scope an operation lists is the one it requires; a write scope includes its resource's read, and sessions:approve includes sessions:read.

agentToken.description: A compact JWS the bridge mints for each request, signed with EdDSA by the session's Ed25519 key, whose kid is that key's base64url public key, whose aud is the server's origin and whose exp is at most 300 seconds away. A request carrying a cookie is refused.

agentApiVersion.name: Agention-Agent-API
agentApiVersion.description: The agent API version the bridge speaks, 1 when absent; a version the server does not serve is refused as unsupported_version.
The agent API version the server speaks.

error.description: Refused. The status follows error.code: invalid_input 400, unsupported_version 400, unauthenticated 401, not_allowed 403, not_found 404, stale 409, request_id_conflict 409, conflict 409, rate_limited 429, storage_full 507, provider_failed 502, internal 500; a body over the server's size limit is invalid_input with 413, and one sent without a Content-Length is invalid_input with 411.

ask.description: The number of the ask this answers.

declined.description: The audience will not answer; a decline carries no picks and no text.

picks.description: The picked suggested answers' indexes, counting from 0.

text.description: Plain text: the audience's own words on the ask, instead of a pick or, where several are allowed, beside its picks; the whole answer to an ask without suggested answers.

suggestions.description: Suggested answers the audience may pick; it may always answer in its own words instead, or beside its picks where several are allowed.

multiple.description: Whether the audience may pick several suggested answers.

answer_by.description: An advisory time to answer by. The server never acts on it.

fallback.description: Plain text: what the requester intends if there is no answer by answer_by.

Ask.description: A question for the audience, open until a message answers it, declining included, a message withdraws it, or its own message is replaced. Only the requester asks. An ask never changes: revise it by replacing its message, which asks again under new numbers, and withdraw it by a withdrawal in a later message, giving the reason.

Effort.description: How long answering takes the audience, when you can judge it: quick (a glance or a short check, about two minutes), under_15m, under_1h, or longer (an hour or more). Leave it out when you cannot judge it.

Impact.description: How the ask affects the requester's work while it is open: blocking (the work the ask is for stops until it is answered, while the requester carries on with other work), assuming (that work goes on under an assumption the message states) or none.

Priority.description: Where the audience should focus, by what delay costs, independent of impact. urgent: something is breaking, costing money or about to miss a real deadline now. high: delay costs real work or time. normal, the default: waiting costs little. low: whenever convenient.

thread.description: A thread of the same session, by its number.

plugin_behind.description: whether the session's latest call stated an older agent API version than the server's, so the server offers features its Agention plugin cannot use; the fix is to update the plugin on the agent's host to its newest release and restart the session. False for a session with no call recorded

description.description: What picking it means, when the label alone does not say.

ask.description: The number of the open ask this withdraws.

reason.description: Plain text: why the ask no longer needs an answer, such as what settled it.

ask.description: The number of the open ask this withdraws.

reason.description: Plain text: why the ask no longer needs an answer, such as what settled it.

WorkOutcome.description: Why you stopped, given only with state stopped: completed when the work is done, withdrawn when the operator called it off, stalled when you cannot go on.

WorkState.description: working while you are doing something now, checking Agention as you go; idle while you have nothing left to do but wait, for the operator's answers, CI or a review, and you still check Agention; stopped once you stop checking Agention, so you will not see new messages until something starts you again. stopped needs an outcome.
